assumptions: L is the Riemann zeta function and xi is its nonzero entire completion
omega>0, nu is a positive integer, and nu*omega>1
Suzuki's K_(omega,nu) is real, continuous, supported in [0,infinity), and has an absolutely convergent high-strip transform
both Fredholm determinants are nonzero for every finite truncation time

exact.causal_multiplier: There is M in H-infinity({Re(s)>0}) with ||M||_infinity=||G||<=1 and L(Gf)(s)=M(s)L(f)(s) for causal f
exact.cofinal_accumulation: If omega_n decreases strictly to 0, an off-line zero rho would force distinct zeros rho-2*omega_n -> rho for all large n, contradicting isolation of zeros of nonzero entire xi
exact.dense_form: D=L2_c(R)={compactly supported L2 functions}; B(f,g)=integral_R integral_R K(x+y)f(y)conj(g(x)) dy dx
exact.determinant_only_equivalence: RH iff there exist strictly decreasing omega_n->0 and positive integers nu_n with nu_n*omega_n>1 such that det(I+/-K_(omega_n,nu_n)[t])!=0 for every n and every t>=0
exact.determinant_to_contraction: det(I+/-K[t])!=0 for every t>=0 implies ||K[t]||<1 for every finite t
exact.global_hankel_extension: B extends uniquely to a bounded Hermitian form on L2(R), represented by a self-adjoint H with ||H||<=1
exact.open_arithmetic_gate: The reduction does not establish the antecedent: one still must prove ||K_(omega_n,nu_n)[t]||<1 for every finite t on a cofinal omega_n sequence without assuming RH or HB
exact.pole_removal: The meromorphic identity theorem makes every apparent pole of the xi quotient in C+ removable
exact.probe_nonvanishing: For q=1_[0,1], L(q)(s)=(1-e^(-s))/s!=0 when Re(s)>0, so the high-strip multiplier identity can be divided by L(q)(s)
exact.reflection_convolution: Jf(x)=f(-x), G=H*J; for f in D, (Gf)(x)=integral_R K(x-y)f(y)dy=(K*f)(x)
exact.shifted_zero: If xi(rho)=0 and Re(rho)>1/2+omega, pole removal at z=-Im(rho)+i*(Re(rho)-1/2-omega) forces xi(rho-2*omega)=0
exact.single_pair_guard: For one fixed omega, holomorphic continuation permits a denominator zero to be canceled by a numerator zero at rho-2*omega; cofinal distinct shifts are essential
exact.terminal_redundancy: Within Suzuki's cofinal criterion, the terminal condition J_(omega_n,nu_n)(t;z,z)->0 follows after the determinant conditions imply RH; it is not an additional logical premise
exact.theta_extension: Theta_tilde(z)=M(-i*z) belongs to H-infinity(C+) with ||Theta_tilde||_infinity<=1 and agrees with [xi(1/2-omega-i*z)/xi(1/2+omega-i*z)]^nu on Im(z)>c
exact.translation_causality: G commutes with every translation and P_a G=P_a G P_a for P_a=1_(-infinity,a); thus G is bounded, translation-invariant, and causal
exact.uniform_form_bound: For f,g in D and t above both supports: B(f,g)=<K[t]f,g>, hence |B(f,g)|<=||f||_2||g||_2

proof_boundary: This artifact proves, modulo the cited standard causal-multiplier theorem, that a cofinal sequence of Suzuki all-time determinant conditions implies RH and hence makes Suzuki's terminal J-limit premise redundant in that cofinal criterion. It does not prove that the determinant conditions hold for zeta, does not rule out common-zero cancellation for one fixed omega, and does not prove RH or Lambda<=0. The determinant-only equivalence is a new corpus theorem candidate and should receive independent expert review before being represented as a published result.

rows.claim: Suzuki's all-time determinant condition supplies a uniform norm-one bound on every compactly supported test pair.
rows.formula: det(I+/-K[t])!=0 for every t>=0 implies ||K[t]||<1 for every finite t
rows.proof_boundary: This uses the continuous compact self-adjoint truncation path from K[0]=0.

rows.claim: The local truncations define one compatible Hankel form on compactly supported functions.
rows.formula: D=L2_c(R)={compactly supported L2 functions}; B(f,g)=integral_R integral_R K(x+y)f(y)conj(g(x)) dy dx
rows.proof_boundary: For each test pair, any t above both supports gives the same value.

rows.claim: All-time strict contractivity bounds the dense Hankel form by one independently of support size.
rows.formula: For f,g in D and t above both supports: B(f,g)=<K[t]f,g>, hence |B(f,g)|<=||f||_2||g||_2
rows.proof_boundary: Strict constants may approach one; only the uniform non-strict bound is used.

rows.claim: The dense form has a unique bounded global Hankel-operator extension.
rows.formula: B extends uniquely to a bounded Hermitian form on L2(R), represented by a self-adjoint H with ||H||<=1
rows.proof_boundary: This is a Riesz-representation argument and does not assume HB or RH.

rows.claim: Reflection turns the global Hankel extension into convolution by Suzuki's supported kernel.
rows.formula: Jf(x)=f(-x), G=H*J; for f in D, (Gf)(x)=integral_R K(x-y)f(y)dy=(K*f)(x)
rows.proof_boundary: Equality is first distributional on compact tests and then holds in L2.

rows.claim: The reflected operator is a bounded causal translation-invariant L2 operator.
rows.formula: G commutes with every translation and P_a G=P_a G P_a for P_a=1_(-infinity,a); thus G is bounded, translation-invariant, and causal
rows.proof_boundary: Causality uses only K(x)=0 for x<0.

rows.claim: The causal L2 multiplier theorem gives a bounded holomorphic transfer function on the right half-plane.
rows.formula: There is M in H-infinity({Re(s)>0}) with ||M||_infinity=||G||<=1 and L(Gf)(s)=M(s)L(f)(s) for causal f
rows.proof_boundary: This is the standard Paley-Wiener multiplier theorem, not an arithmetic assumption.

rows.claim: The transfer function is Suzuki's absolutely convergent high-strip Laplace transform.
rows.proof_boundary: For q=1_[0,1], L(q)(s)=(1-e^(-s))/s!=0 when Re(s)>0, so the high-strip multiplier identity can be divided by L(q)(s)

rows.claim: All-time determinant nonvanishing forces the meromorphic xi quotient to have a contractive H-infinity extension to C+.
rows.formula: Theta_tilde(z)=M(-i*z) belongs to H-infinity(C+) with ||Theta_tilde||_infinity<=1 and agrees with [xi(1/2-omega-i*z)/xi(1/2+omega-i*z)]^nu on Im(z)>c
rows.proof_boundary: The equality starts on Im(z)>c and extends meromorphically by identity.

rows.claim: Every upper-half-plane denominator zero is canceled by a numerator zero of at least the same multiplicity.
rows.formula: The meromorphic identity theorem makes every apparent pole of the xi quotient in C+ removable
rows.proof_boundary: Cancellation need not make the underlying E function Hermite-Biehler for one fixed omega.

rows.claim: A zero to the right of the shifted critical line propagates left by exactly 2 omega.
rows.formula: If xi(rho)=0 and Re(rho)>1/2+omega, pole removal at z=-Im(rho)+i*(Re(rho)-1/2-omega) forces xi(rho-2*omega)=0
rows.proof_boundary: Only existence, not multiplicity, is needed in the cofinal argument.

rows.claim: A cofinal sequence of distinct shifts rules out every zero to the right of the critical line.
rows.formula: If omega_n decreases strictly to 0, an off-line zero rho would force distinct zeros rho-2*omega_n -> rho for all large n, contradicting isolation of zeros of nonzero entire xi
rows.proof_boundary: The functional equation then rules out zeros to the left.

rows.claim: Suzuki's cofinal RH criterion can be sharpened by deleting its terminal-kernel premise.
rows.formula: RH iff there exist strictly decreasing omega_n->0 and positive integers nu_n with nu_n*omega_n>1 such that det(I+/-K_(omega_n,nu_n)[t])!=0 for every n and every t>=0
rows.proof_boundary: The implication from RH is Suzuki's conditional all-time contraction theorem; the reverse implication is rows sdr_01 through sdr_12.

rows.claim: For a cofinal family satisfying the determinant premise, Suzuki's terminal limit follows after RH and is logically redundant.
rows.formula: Within Suzuki's cofinal criterion, the terminal condition J_(omega_n,nu_n)(t;z,z)->0 follows after the determinant conditions imply RH; it is not an additional logical premise
rows.proof_boundary: This does not derive the terminal limit directly from one fixed determinant family.

rows.claim: A single omega is insufficient because common-zero cancellation can survive.
rows.formula: For one fixed omega, holomorphic continuation permits a denominator zero to be canceled by a numerator zero at rho-2*omega; cofinal distinct shifts are essential
rows.proof_boundary: Do not promote one fixed contractive family to a zero-free half-plane without an extra no-common-zero theorem.

rows.claim: The determinant-only equivalence isolates one remaining Suzuki-side arithmetic gate.
rows.formula: The reduction does not establish the antecedent: one still must prove ||K_(omega_n,nu_n)[t]||<1 for every finite t on a cofinal omega_n sequence without assuming RH or HB
rows.proof_boundary: No proof of this all-time signed contraction gate is presently in the corpus.
